1848: In order to report sequencing data evidence for both variant and non-variant positions in the genome, the VCF specification allows to represent blocks of reference-only calls in a single record using the $<$*$>$ allele and the FORMAT LEN field.
1849: The convention adopted here is to represent reference evidence as likelihoods against an unknown alternate allele represented as $<$*$>$.
1850: Think of this as the likelihood for reference as compared to any other possible alternate allele (both SNP, indel, or otherwise).
1852: Positions implicitly called by a preceding $<$*$>$ for a sample must have $GT$ set to the missing value (`.') and have no FORMAT fields other than $LAA$ present.

findings.finding: A VCF sample may represent a mixture of multiple genomes. The SAMPLE metadata Genomes/Mixture/Description structure provides the model; sample-level read counts and later genome-level deconvolution/copy-number estimates are distinct analytical representations. The tables are examples, not mandatory deconvolution procedures.

PEDIGREE can express asexual/clonal derivation using Original, and a general line can name one or more ancestors. The specification says suggested/possible representation in some clauses; do not convert every described cancer workflow into mandatory metadata.

Haplotype IDs are unique across the germline genome and conserved along clonal lineages despite mutations, rearrangements or recombination. On duplication, one copy retains the original ID and additional copies become novel haplotypes with their own unique IDs and shared haplotype ancestor.

The <*> allele and FORMAT LEN support reference-only blocks. At positions implicitly called by a preceding <*> for a sample, GT is missing and no FORMAT fields other than LAA are present. If LAA is present at a reference-block start for a sample, <*> is included in that sample's LAA despite GT=0/0.

The text attributes reference blocks to gVCF, notes limitations of INFO END for multi-sample variable block lengths, states <NON_REF> should be treated as an alias of <*>, and infers missing FORMAT LEN from INFO END when present. The source modal should be preserved; this is a compatibility convention, not a new core allele grammar.

The worked records demonstrate FORMAT LEN and redundant INFO END, including records with and without <*>, and the following prose says base-modification annotations in a reference block apply to all applicable covered bases.
